message.content:
In this Go repository (a "memos" note-taking app server, path server/ and proto/ etc.), I need to find which RPC handler methods (in server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go or similar) can transitively trigger an outbound HTTP request to a URL that is configured by the user (e.g., webhook URL, link/OpenGraph metadata fetch URL, OIDC/identity-provider URL, etc.), and find the single shared/common function where these different code paths converge before actually making the HTTP request (e.g., a shared "doHTTPRequest" or webhook dispatcher function).

Please investigate:
1. grep for `http.Client`, `http.Get`, `http.Post`, `http.NewRequest`, `.Do(` across the server/ directory (Go code) to find all places that issue outbound HTTP requests.
2. For each such call site, trace backward to find which RPC/connect service handler method (in connect_services.go, methods like .CreateUserWebhook(), .GetLinkMetadata(), .CreateIdentityProvider(), .UpdateIdentityProvider(), .TestInstanceEmailSetting(), .Transcribe(), webhook-on-memo-create hooks, etc.) can reach it.
3. Determine whether there is a single shared function (e.g. a webhook delivery function, or a generic URL-fetch helper) where multiple of these RPC paths converge before the actual outbound request is made.
4. Also check for any webhook-triggering code that fires on memo create/update/delete events (this is a common one in memos-like apps) - look in server/ for files with "webhook" in the name.

Report back: 
- the list of outbound HTTP call sites (file:line) 
- for each, which RPC handler(s) can reach it and roughly how (call chain)
- the single convergence function (file:line and name) where paths join before the HTTP request is actually sent, if one exists.

Be concrete with file paths and line numbers. This is for security/architecture documentation purposes.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text: Confirmed: email uses SMTP (`internal/email`), not HTTP — out of scope. Only one identity provider type (OAuth2) exists under `internal/idp`. Now I have a complete picture. Let me do a final check on `user_service_identities.go` (CreateLinkedIdentity) to confirm its exact call chain matches SignIn's.

All confirmed. I now have the full picture.

## Outbound HTTP call sites (file:line)

| # | Call site | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go:126` (`http.NewRequest`) + `:152` (`safeClient.Do(req)`) | Webhook dispatch (`Post`/`PostAsync`) |
| 2 | `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:85` (`http.NewRequestWithContext`) + `:91` (`client.Do(req)`) | OAuth2/OIDC `UserInfo` fetch |
| 3 | `/bench/home/work/internal/httpgetter/html_meta.go:141` (`httpClient.Get(urlStr)`) | HTML/OpenGraph metadata fetch (`GetHTMLMeta`) |
| 4 | `/bench/home/work/internal/httpgetter/image.go:21` (`http.Get(urlStr)`) | Image fetch (`GetImage`) — defined but **not currently called** from `server/` (dead/unused from the RPC layer as far as I can find) |
| 5 | Indirect/SDK-mediated: `internal/ai/stt/openai/openai.go` (via `openaisdk.NewClient(...WithHTTPClient(options.HTTPClient))`, actual request built inside the `openai-go` SDK) | Transcription via OpenAI-compatible endpoint (user-configured `Endpoint`) |
| 6 | Indirect/SDK-mediated: `internal/ai/audiollm/gemini/gemini.go` (via `genai.NewClient(...HTTPClient: options.HTTPClient...)`, request built inside `google.golang.org/genai` SDK) | Transcription via Gemini-compatible endpoint (user-configured `Endpoint`) |

Note: `TestInstanceEmailSetting` (`server/router/api/v1/instance_service.go:256`) uses SMTP (`internal/email`), not HTTP — out of scope despite also taking a user-configured server address.

## Call chains from RPC handlers

**A. Webhook dispatch → `internal/webhook.Post`/`PostAsync` (webhook.go:126/152)**
- `ConnectServiceHandler.CreateMemo/UpdateMemo/DeleteMemo` (connect_services.go:306/330/338) → `APIV1Service.CreateMemo` (memo_service.go:70, dispatch at line 157) / `UpdateMemo` (via `memo_update_helpers.go:67`) / `DeleteMemo` (memo_service.go:518, dispatch at line 562) → `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook`/`DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook`/`DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` (memo_service_webhooks.go:15/20/25) → `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` (memo_service_webhooks.go:48) → `webhook.PostAsync` (memo_service_webhooks.go:71).
- `ConnectServiceHandler.CreateMemoComment` (connect_services.go:378) → `APIV1Service` comment handler (`memo_service_comments.go:119`) → `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` (memo_service_webhooks.go:30) → `webhook.PostAsync` (memo_service_webhooks.go:43).
- Note: `CreateUserWebhook`/`UpdateUserWebhook` (connect_services.go:248/256, `user_service_webhooks.go`) only *register* a webhook URL and run `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`) — they do **not** themselves issue the outbound request; the request only fires later on a memo event.

**B. OAuth2/OIDC UserInfo fetch → `oauth2.UserInfo` (oauth2.go:91)**
- `ConnectServiceHandler.SignIn` → `APIV1Service.SignIn` (`auth_service.go:51`, SSO branch at line 78) → `resolveSSOIdentity` (`auth_service_sso.go:104`) → `oauth2.NewIdentityProvider(...).UserInfo(ctx, token)` (`auth_service_sso.go:121,130`).
- `ConnectServiceHandler.CreateLinkedIdentity` (connect_services.go:192) → `APIV1Service.CreateLinkedIdentity` (`user_service_identities.go:39`, line 56) → same `resolveSSOIdentity` → same `oauth2...UserInfo`.
- (`CreateIdentityProvider`/`UpdateIdentityProvider`, `idp_service.go`, just persist the IdP config to the store — no outbound call at creation time; the URL is only actually hit later when a user signs in via that provider.)

**C. Link/OpenGraph metadata fetch → `httpgetter.GetHTMLMeta` (html_meta.go:141)**
- `ConnectServiceHandler.GetLinkMetadata` / `BatchGetLinkMetadata` (connect_services.go:450/458) → `APIV1Service.GetLinkMetadata`/`BatchGetLinkMetadata` (`memo_service_link_metadata.go:14/19`) → shared helper `getLinkMetadata` (`memo_service_link_metadata.go:41`) → `fetchHTMLMeta(url)` (var assigned to `httpgetter.GetHTMLMeta` at `memo_service.go:28`) → `httpClient.Get` (html_meta.go:141).

**D. Transcription → AI provider endpoint**
- `ConnectServiceHandler.Transcribe` (connect_services.go:518) → `APIV1Service.Transcribe` (`ai_service.go:48`) → `resolveAIProvider` (uses admin-configured `Endpoint` from `InstanceAISetting`) → `transcribeViaSTT`/`transcribeViaAudioLLM` (ai_service.go:123/151) → `sttopenai.New(...).Transcribe` / `audiollmgemini.New(...).GenerateFromAudio`, which hand off to vendor SDKs that build/send the actual HTTP request internally.

## Convergence points

There is **no single convergence function shared across all these paths** — the codebase deliberately keeps three/four independent HTTP egress points, each with its own (differing) SSRF-hardening:

1. **Webhook path** converges at `Post` in `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (called by both `Post` itself and via the async wrapper `PostAsync` at line 184). All three memo-event dispatchers and the comment dispatcher funnel through the single shared helper `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` (memo_service_webhooks.go:48) → `webhook.PostAsync` → `Post` → `safeClient.Do(req)` (webhook.go:152), which uses a shared `safeClient` (webhook.go:32) with SSRF-guarding `safeDialContext` (webhook.go:59).
2. **Link-metadata path** converges at `getLinkMetadata` in `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_link_metadata.go:41`, which both `GetLinkMetadata` and `BatchGetLinkMetadata` call before reaching `httpgetter.GetHTMLMeta` → `httpClient.Get` (html_meta.go:141), guarded by its own SSRF logic (`secureDialContext`, html_meta.go:51, and `validateURL`, html_meta.go:108).
3. **SSO/OIDC path** converges at `resolveSSOIdentity` in `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:104`, shared by `SignIn` and `CreateLinkedIdentity`, before reaching `oauth2.IdentityProvider.UserInfo` (oauth2.go:83) — this path has **no SSRF/private-IP protection** (plain `&http.Client{Timeout: ...}`, oauth2.go:84), unlike the webhook and link-metadata paths.
4. **AI transcription path** is separate again — it doesn't go through either shared function above; it goes through vendor SDK clients (`openai-go`, `google.golang.org/genai`) using a plain per-call `http.Client{Timeout: ...}` (`internal/ai/stt/options.go:29`, `internal/ai/audiollm/options.go:29`) with **no SSRF protection**, hitting an admin-configurable `Endpoint`.

So: within each feature area there is a converging helper (`webhook.Post`, `getLinkMetadata`, `resolveSSOIdentity`), but there is **no single app-wide "doHTTPRequest" dispatcher** that all four RPC-triggerable outbound-HTTP paths share. That is itself a notable architectural/security finding: SSRF protections were added independently to `internal/webhook` (`safeDialContext`) and `internal/httpgetter` (`secureDialContext`/`validateURL`), but the OAuth2 UserInfo fetch (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`) and the AI transcription SDK clients (`internal/ai/stt`, `internal/ai/audiollm`) have no equivalent private-IP/redirect guarding, despite also being reachable via user/admin-supplied URLs (`UserInfoUrl` in the IdP config, `Endpoint` in the AI provider config).
